brief: What happened in round 1: WP270 rewrote privacy §7's ‘Meeting recordings’ bullet in EN/ES/CA and the release notes. Its first check found that the 7-day sentence named only a recording cut off before Stop and left out a quiet Stop the app also asks about (R1-WP270-1, now WEB-2003); its one fix replaced that sentence with ‘A recording the app asks you about, and that you leave unanswered, becomes a note 7 days after it asks.’ and the second check confirmed WEB-1901, WEB-1902, WEB-1903 and WEB-2003 fixed (`verify-r1-WP270-2.md`). But the fix's longer Spanish sentence left the bullet's last line as the single word «reuniones.» on a 390 px phone, light and dark (R1-WP270-2, now WEB-2004), so the package was shelved unmerged as `unmerged-WP270.patch`. The main checkout still has the old, false bullet. This package lands that work and fixes the one-word line. It is still a correction inside the owner's sign-off for version 2026-11-05: the version stays 2026-11-05 (see the decisions convention).

Step 1, land WP270. In your copy's root run `git apply /home/claude/TaskFlowWeb/.claude/ux-web/runs/2026-11-05-pages/unmerged-WP270.patch` (the run folder is untracked, so use this absolute path; on the owner's PC it is the same file under the website root). `git apply --check` passed against the main checkout after WP271's merge on 2026-11-05. Step 2, WEB-2004 (S1). In `src/content/legal/es.ts:126`, the bullet's last sentence «Eliminar tu cuenta borra sus reuniones.» becomes «Eliminar tu cuenta borra sus\u00a0reuniones.»: a no-break space between «sus» and «reuniones.», written as the escape `\u00a0` inside the string, the way WEB-1609 wrote `Google\u00a0LLC` in `src/content/site/es.ts:41`. Nothing else in the sentence changes. Why this and not `text-wrap: pretty` on `.legal-body li` (`src/styles/legal.css:225`), the verifier's alternative: that would re-wrap every list item on all three legal pages in all three languages, outside this package's lines and beyond what round 2 can re-check; the no-break space is the site's own precedent and stays on the package's line. Don't touch `legal.css`.
